info.title: Songlinks API
info.description:
Look up a songwriter by name and get back the people who write under it: registration records grouped into one
person each, the evidence for every grouping, and a person ID where one has been issued.

> **Beta.** Unverified machine output, from a dated snapshot of registration data (every answer's `mlc_snapshot`
> gives its date). Some answers are wrong and some are incomplete, and none has been checked by a person. Not for
> rights or royalty decisions. The API may change, be rate-limited or stop without notice.

## Quick start

No key and no sign-up. Look up a name:

    curl "https://api.songlinks.to/v1/lookup?name=mark+hoppus"

Each person in `candidates` carries a `persistent_id` when an ID has been issued. Read everything that ID holds,
including its works:

    curl "https://api.songlinks.to/v1/person/SLP-ZYM7-GD3E-S"

On [/v1/docs](/v1/docs) every endpoint below can be run from the page: open it, fill in the parameters and choose
**Execute**.

## SDKs

The official TypeScript and JavaScript SDK calls these endpoints with types generated from this API's OpenAPI document,
typed errors, retries that honour `Retry-After`, and paging through a person's works. It runs on Node 18+, in browsers,
Deno and Bun, with no dependencies:

    npm install songlinks

Its README, on [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/songlinks), has the examples and links its source.

## Two questions, two endpoints

| Endpoint | Question | Answered from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/lookup` | Who writes under this name? | The records matching the name, grouped for this request |
| `GET /v1/person/{person_id}` | What does this person ID hold? | The grouping stored when the ID was issued, and its history since |
| `GET /v1/writers?ipi=...` | Who holds each of these IPI name numbers, and are their works split? | The same stored groupings, up to 50 numbers at once |

The two can differ. A lookup sees only the records its spelling of the name reaches, so a stored person can hold
records a lookup does not show. A candidate's `records_not_in_this_answer` counts them.

## Reading a lookup

1. **Check `answer` first.** `rejected` means the name could not be resolved, and `rejection.code` says why. A
   rejection is an answer and comes back with HTTP 200, not an error.
2. **`candidates`** has one entry per person. Its `records` are the registrations grouped into that person, `works`
   counts their distinct works, and `evidence` says why each pair of records was joined.
3. **`review`** lists pairs of records that were **not** joined: the model was unsure, or a rule held them apart.
   Show them apart from `candidates`, never as part of a person.
4. **`links`** lists records registered under another name, such as a stage name, next to one of this lookup's
   records. It is a different claim from "same person", and its works are not counted in `works`.
5. **`truncated: true`** means more records matched than one lookup groups (`provenance.max_candidates`). Treat the
   answer as partial.
6. **`ref`** (`c1`, `c2`, ...) names a candidate inside one response and nowhere else: another spelling of the name
   can group the records differently. To keep a reference to a person, keep `persistent_id`, which is null for
   people with no ID.

| `rejection.code` | Meaning | What to show |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `single-token` | The name is one word, which is not searched | Ask for a full name |
| `no-match` | Nothing matched closely enough | `nearest`, as spelling suggestions |
| `publishers-only` | Every match is registered only as a publisher or administrator | `set_aside_roles` says which |

## Person IDs

A person ID looks like `SLP-ZYM7-GD3E-S`: eight characters in two groups, then a check character that catches most
typos. Case does not matter, and I, L and O are read as 1, 1 and 0; the API redirects any such spelling to the
canonical one.

* **`prerelease: true`**: the ID may stop resolving, or later point at a different person, without notice. Do not
  store it.
* **`prerelease: false`**: a released ID. If a released ID is merged into another, it redirects there permanently.

| `GET /v1/person/{person_id}` returns | When |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | The person, with one page of works |
| 307 | A merged prerelease ID. `Location` is the survivor |
| 308 | A non-canonical spelling of an ID, or a merged released ID |
| 404 | No person has this ID: never issued, mistyped, or a wrong check character |
| 410 | The ID was issued and later withdrawn. Its number is never issued again |

A person has two lists of records. **`records`** are members, and their works make up `works` and `works_list`.
**`possible`** records may be the same person but are not members, are never counted, and may belong to someone else.

Works come a page at a time, most-recorded first (`works_list.ordered_by`: `recordings` where the recording counts
are available, otherwise `coded`, which puts works carrying an ISWC first). Pass `works_list.next_offset` as `works_offset` to get the next page; it
is null on the last one. `works_list.total` is always the full count.

## Status codes and errors

| Status | Body | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | The answer | Includes a rejected lookup |
| 400 | `Error` | `too_many` or `no_numbers`: a `/v1/writers` list over 50 numbers, or with none |
| 307, 308 | None | A redirect, on `/v1/person` only. Most HTTP clients follow it |
| 404 | `Error` | `not_found`: no person has this ID |
| 410 | `PersonWithdrawnResponse` | A withdrawn person ID |
| 422 | `HTTPValidationError` | A parameter is missing or out of range; `detail` says which |
| 429 | `RateLimited` | Over a per-caller limit. Wait for the `Retry-After` header's seconds |
| 500 | `Error` | `internal`: the request failed. The cause is never returned |
| 503 | `Error` | `not_ready` (starting) or `busy`. Retry after a few seconds |

Branch on `error`, not `message`: the wording of `message` may change.

## Limits

There is no key and no quota. The service is small, so **send one request at a time** rather than many in parallel.

A per-caller limit can be switched on. While it is on, every answer carries `rate_limit` and an
`X-RateLimit-Remaining` header, and a request over the limit gets 429 with `Retry-After`. While it is off,
`rate_limit` is null and the header is absent.

## Provenance

Every lookup carries `provenance`. If you keep an answer, keep `provenance.model_md5` and `provenance.code_commit`
with it: together they identify what produced it. `GET /v1/version` returns the same values without a lookup, and
`version`, the release.

Society numbers in the examples on this page are shortened. Real responses carry all 11 digits.

get.description: Answers `{"status": "ok"}` while the service is up. It does not check the data, so a 200 here does not promise that a lookup will succeed.
The release, model and code serving the API, and the settings every lookup uses, without running one. Record it with any answer you keep.

get.summary: Look up a songwriter by name
get.description:
Groups the registration records that match `name` into people, and says why each group was formed.

Check `answer` first. `candidates` is an answer, and so is `rejected`, which comes with HTTP 200 and a `rejection`
saying why. **Reading a lookup**, at the top of this page, goes through the rest of the response.

parameters.name: name

schema.description: A songwriter's full name, for example `mark hoppus`. A one-word name is not searched: it comes back rejected, with `single-token`.
schema.title: Name

parameters.name: routes

schema.description: Extra routes to run with the lookup, comma-separated. `catalogue`, the default, fills `links` with records registered under another name. `none` skips it, and the lookup is faster.

schema.description: How sure the model must be to join two records, from 0.5 to 0.99. Higher gives fewer, surer joins. The value used is echoed in `query.threshold`.
schema.title: Threshold

parameters.name: song

schema.description: Optional: the title of a song this writer wrote, for example `all the small things`. When several people share the name, `song_match` says which of them has a work by that title, including songs never recorded. It points at people already in the answer; it does not find anyone the name did not.

get.summary: Watch one pair of records decided
get.description: The decision for two party records, in the shape the /learn page plays: whether the pair passed the evidence gate, the questions it was asked on its way through one chain (as kinds of evidence, in plain words), its answer to each as a word, which way it went, the size of each push as a word, and the zone the needle settled in. No score, cut, count or figure: those are not published. Read-only. Beta: the shape of this response may change.

get.description:
Returns what a person ID holds: its member records and why each was linked, the `possible` records kept apart, the
ID's history, and one page of works.

This reads the stored person; it does not run a lookup. An ID that was never issued is a 404, and so is a malformed
ID or one with a wrong check character.

A merged ID redirects to the survivor: 307 while it is prerelease, 308 once released. A non-canonical spelling
redirects to the canonical one with 308. **Person IDs**, at the top of this page, has the whole table.

get.summary: Check a list of writers by IPI name number
get.description:
For each IPI name number in `ipi`, the stored person who holds it, and how that person's works divide between their
main number and every other registration: `works_elsewhere` counts the works registered only under another spelling
of the name or another IPI name number.

This reads the stored persons; it runs no lookup, so it answers the same way each time until the groupings change.
Up to 50 numbers per request, after duplicates are removed; more is a 400 with `too_many`. An entry that is not an IPI
name number comes back with `status: invalid` and does not fail the request. A number no person holds comes back
`none`, which is the ordinary answer for a publisher's number.

`summary.with_works_elsewhere` is the number of writers in the list with works registered under another spelling or
number.

parameters.name: ipi

schema.description: IPI name numbers, comma-separated, up to 50. Leading zeros may be left off, and spaces and dashes inside a number are ignored. Semicolons and line breaks also separate numbers; a space does not.
schema.title: Ipi

parameters.description: IPI name numbers, comma-separated, up to 50. Leading zeros may be left off, and spaces and dashes inside a number are ignored. Semicolons and line breaks also separate numbers; a space does not.

checked.summary: Three entries: a person, nobody, not a number

value.message: at most 50 IPI name numbers per request; this one has 51

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: where the build ran, such as `production`; diagnostic

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: when the build started, as an ISO 8601 timestamp

finished_at.title: Finished At
finished_at.description: when the build finished, as an ISO 8601 timestamp

model_version.title: Model Version
model_version.description: identifies the model the build used

code_commit.title: Code Commit
code_commit.description: identifies the code the build ran

code_dirty.title: Code Dirty
code_dirty.description: true if the build ran with uncommitted changes; diagnostic

mlc_snapshot.title: Mlc Snapshot
mlc_snapshot.description: the date of the registration-data release the build read, YYYY-MM-DD. Null when that load is undated: never a guess

BuildRef.title: BuildRef
BuildRef.description: A build: the automatic run that groups records into people and issues IDs.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: names this candidate inside this response only (`c1`, `c2`, ...). Another spelling of the name can group the records differently, so never store it

persistent_id.title: Persistent Id
persistent_id.description: the person ID, `SLP-XXXX-XXXX-C`, or null when none has been issued, or when the records belong to more than one person (see `stored_persons`). Null is common

prerelease.title: Prerelease
prerelease.description: true: the ID may stop resolving, or later point at a different person, without notice, so do not store it. False: a released ID. Null when there is no ID

person_state.title: Person State
person_state.description: the stored person's `state`; null when there is no ID

redirected_from.title: Redirected From
redirected_from.description: when a record's ID has since been merged into this one, that older ID

person_records.title: Person Records
person_records.description: how many registrations the stored person holds as theirs (its member records); null when there is no ID

records_not_in_this_answer.title: Records Not In This Answer
records_not_in_this_answer.description: member records the stored person holds that this lookup did not reach. Read the person to see them

ipi_name_numbers.title: Ipi Name Numbers
ipi_name_numbers.description: every distinct IPI name number in `records`

works.title: Works
works.description: distinct works across `records`: a work registered under two of them counts once, so this can be less than their sum. It counts every record this lookup grouped, so it can be more than the stored person's own `works`, which counts only the records the person ID holds

records.title: Records
records.description: the registration records grouped into this person, most works first

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: one entry per pair of records joined

main_ipi_name_number.title: Main Ipi Name Number
main_ipi_name_number.description: the IPI name number most of this person's works are registered under: the one whose records hold the most works. Null when no record has one

works_on_main_ipi.title: Works On Main Ipi
works_on_main_ipi.description: distinct works on the records carrying `main_ipi_name_number`. `works` minus this is how many works are held only by the person's other registrations, under another number or none. Null when `main_ipi_name_number` is

stored_persons.title: Stored Persons
stored_persons.description: the person IDs this candidate's records belong to. Usually one, the same as `persistent_id`. Two or more mean Songlinks' person records hold these registrations as different people, so the candidate has no single `persistent_id`: read each record's own ID

Cluster.title: Cluster
Cluster.description: One person, as this lookup groups them: the registration records judged to be the same songwriter.

error.title: Error
error.description: `too_many` or `no_numbers` (400), `not_found` (404), `internal` (500), or `not_ready` or `busy` (503). Branch on this

message.title: Message
message.description: a short sentence for people; its wording may change

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
The body of a 400, 404, 500 or 503 response. It never carries detail about what failed. A malformed parameter
(an empty name, a threshold out of range) is answered 422 instead, with a `detail` list saying which parameter and
why.

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: `same_ipi_name_number`: both records carry the same IPI name number. `model`: the model judged them to be the same person

probability.title: Probability
probability.description: the model's calibrated probability that the two records are one person, from 0 to 1

shared.title: Shared
shared.description: what the two records have in common, under `co_writers`, `publishers` and `administrators`, each `{"count": n, "rarest": [names]}`. `rarest` lists the least common shared names, which say the most; names shared by a very large number of writers are left out. A key may be absent

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description: Why two records in a candidate were joined.

ipi_name_number.title: Ipi Name Number
ipi_name_number.description: the linked record's IPI name number, or null

grade.title: Grade
grade.description: `checked`: the two people share no registered work, so the link is not a co-writer's. `co-writers too`: they share works, as bandmates do, and the link is weaker

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: how close together the two records were registered; 1 is adjacent

works.title: Works
works.description: works registered under the linked record

from_record.title: From Record
from_record.description: the record in this lookup the link starts from

forward.title: Forward
forward.description: `[credited, recorded]`: of the linked record's works that have a recording, how many credit `from_name` as the artist

back.title: Back
back.description: `[credited, recorded]`: of `from_record`'s works that have a recording, how many credit `name` as the artist

Link.title: Link
Link.description:
A record registered under another name next to one of this lookup's records: a stage name and a legal name, for
example. A different claim from a candidate: nothing here is joined, and its works are not counted in `works`.

answer.title: Answer
answer.description: either `candidates` or `rejected`. When it is `rejected`, `rejection` says why

rejection.description: why the lookup stopped; null unless `answer` is `rejected`

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: the people the name could be, one entry each; empty when `answer` is `rejected`

review.title: Review
review.description: pairs of records held apart; never part of a candidate

links.title: Links
links.description: records registered under another name next to this lookup's; filled only when `routes` includes `catalogue`

records_considered.title: Records Considered
records_considered.description: records grouped into this answer; at most `provenance.max_candidates`

records_passed.title: Records Passed
records_passed.description: records that matched closely enough to be considered

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: true when more records matched than one lookup groups (`records_passed` > `records_considered`). The answer is partial

persons_resolved.title: Persons Resolved
persons_resolved.description: how many candidates carry a person ID

song_match.description: which candidates wrote the song; null unless a `song` was sent and the lookup found candidates

rate_limit.description: your remaining allowance; null when no per-caller limit is in force. The edge's per-address limit (about 100 requests per 5 minutes, 20 from VPNs and hosting networks) is separate and not counted here

LookupResponse.title: LookupResponse
LookupResponse.description: The answer to one lookup. Check `answer` first.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `issued`, `released` (no longer prerelease), `record_added`, `record_removed`, `record_moved`, `evidence_changed`, `merged`, `split`, `wiped` (a prerelease ID withdrawn) or `flagged`

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: the ID the entry is about; for `merged`, the ID that now redirects

other_person_id.title: Other Person Id
other_person_id.description: for `merged`, the ID it redirects to

party_record_id.title: Party Record Id
party_record_id.description: the record concerned, where there is one

build_id.title: Build Id
build_id.description: the build that made the change, where there is one

decided_by.title: Decided By
decided_by.description: `build` for an automatic build; otherwise who decided

PersonEvent.title: PersonEvent
PersonEvent.description: One entry in the ID's history. History is only ever added to, never edited.

issued_by.description: the build that issued the ID

latest_build.description: the most recent build to group these records

mlc_snapshot.title: Mlc Snapshot
mlc_snapshot.description: the date of the registration-data release this answer read, YYYY-MM-DD. Null when that load is undated: never a guess

api_model_md5.title: Api Model Md5
api_model_md5.description: the model serving lookups; not the model that grouped this person

api_code_commit.title: Api Code Commit
api_code_commit.description: the code that served this response

PersonProvenance.title: PersonProvenance
PersonProvenance.description:
What grouped these records, and what served this response: two different things. `issued_by` and `latest_build`
grouped the records. `api_model_md5` and `api_code_commit` only served the response, and decided nothing in it.

party_record_id.title: Party Record Id
party_record_id.description: identifies this record in the registration data

name.title: Name
name.description: the name as registered; null only if the record is no longer in the registration data

key_name.title: Key Name
key_name.description: the part of the name the record is filed under, usually the surname

names_before_key_name.title: Names Before Key Name
names_before_key_name.description: the rest of the name, usually given names

ipi_name_number.title: Ipi Name Number
ipi_name_number.description: the IPI name number, or null

works.title: Works
works.description: this record's own works, counted once each

link.title: Link
link.description: `anchor`: the record the ID was issued on. `asserted`: a member. `possible`: perhaps this person, but not a member

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: why the record was linked: `same_ipi` (the same IPI name number as a member), `ipi` (the anchor's own IPI name number), `model` (the model's judgement), `corroborated` (confirmed by an independent outside source) or `verdict` (decided by a person)

score.title: Score
score.description: the model's calibrated probability, where the model was involved

decided_by.title: Decided By
decided_by.description: `build` for an automatic build; otherwise who decided

build_id.title: Build Id
build_id.description: the build that linked the record

member_of.title: Member Of
member_of.description: the other person ID that holds this record as a member, or null; always null on `records`, whose holder is this person

member_of_prerelease.title: Member Of Prerelease
member_of_prerelease.description: whether that person ID is prerelease

PersonRecord.title: PersonRecord
PersonRecord.description: One registration record on a stored person, and how it was linked.

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: `SLP-XXXX-XXXX-C`; the last character is a check character

prerelease.title: Prerelease
prerelease.description: true: the ID may stop resolving, or later point at a different person, without notice, so do not store it. False: a released ID

state.title: State
state.description: `active`. `split`: part of the group was separated and this ID kept the anchor. `anchor_missing`: the anchor record is no longer in the registration data; the ID stays

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: what the ID qualifies on now: `same_ipi` (members share a IPI name number), `ipi` (the anchor's IPI name number and catalogue), `corroborated` (a member's IPI name number confirmed by an independent outside source) or `human` (decided by a person). It can change after issue; `issued_evidence` is what it was issued on

issued_evidence.title: Issued Evidence
issued_evidence.description: what the ID was issued on, one of the `evidence` values, from its history. Null when the history does not record it

issued_at.title: Issued At
issued_at.description: when the ID was issued, ISO 8601

released_at.title: Released At
released_at.description: when it was released; null while prerelease

redirected_from.title: Redirected From
redirected_from.description: the merged ID this request was redirected from, when the history confirms it

merged_from.title: Merged From
merged_from.description: IDs merged into this one; each redirects here

name.title: Name
name.description: the name to show for this person

names.title: Names
names.description: every distinct registered name among the members

ipi_name_numbers.title: Ipi Name Numbers
ipi_name_numbers.description: every distinct IPI name number among the members

works.title: Works
works.description: distinct works across member records; `possible` records are not counted

main_ipi_name_number.title: Main Ipi Name Number
main_ipi_name_number.description: this person's main IPI name number: the one on the record their ID was created around (the record whose `link` is `anchor`). It never changes. It is usually, but not always, the number most of their works are under. Null when no member has one

works_on_main_ipi.title: Works On Main Ipi
works_on_main_ipi.description: distinct works on the member records carrying `main_ipi_name_number`. `works` minus this is how many works only the person's other registrations hold. Null when `main_ipi_name_number` is

possible.title: Possible
possible.description: NOT members: perhaps this person, never counted

works_list.description: one page of works; ask for more with `works_offset`

history.title: History
history.description: every change to this ID, oldest first

rate_limit.description: your remaining allowance; null when no per-caller limit is in force. The edge's per-address limit (about 100 requests per 5 minutes, 20 from VPNs and hosting networks) is separate and not counted here

provenance.description: what grouped these records, and what served the response

PersonResponse.title: PersonResponse
PersonResponse.description:
A stored person: what a person ID holds, not a fresh lookup. `records` are its members, the registrations the ID
holds as this person's. `possible` lists registrations that may also be theirs; they are not members, are never
counted in `works`, and may belong to someone else.

history.title: History
history.description: every change to this ID, oldest first

PersonWithdrawnResponse.title: PersonWithdrawnResponse
PersonWithdrawnResponse.description: HTTP 410: this ID was issued and later withdrawn. This person ID will never be issued to anyone else.

mlc_work_id.title: Mlc Work Id
mlc_work_id.description: identifies the work in the registration data

iswc.title: Iswc
iswc.description: the ISWC, or null when the work has none

records.title: Records
records.description: the member records the work is registered under

PersonWork.title: PersonWork
PersonWork.description: One work registered under one or more of the person's member records (the registrations the ID holds).

model_md5.title: Model Md5
model_md5.description: identifies the model that grouped the records

code_commit.title: Code Commit
code_commit.description: identifies the code that produced the answer

mlc_snapshot.title: Mlc Snapshot
mlc_snapshot.description: the date of the registration-data release this answer read, YYYY-MM-DD. Null when that load is undated: never a guess

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: the threshold this answer used; see the `threshold` parameter

review_threshold.title: Review Threshold
review_threshold.description: the lowest probability at which an unjoined pair is listed in `review`

max_candidates.title: Max Candidates
max_candidates.description: the most records one lookup groups; see `truncated`

latency_ms.title: Latency Ms
latency_ms.description: time taken to produce the answer, in milliseconds

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description: What produced this answer. Keep `model_md5` and `code_commit` with any answer you store.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: the threshold used, as sent or defaulted

song.title: Song
song.description: the song as sent; null when none was

Query.title: Query
Query.description: The question that was answered, echoed back.

remaining.title: Remaining
remaining.description: requests left in the current window

window_seconds.title: Window Seconds
window_seconds.description: the length of the window, in seconds

RateLimit.title: RateLimit
RateLimit.description: Your remaining allowance under a per-caller limit.

window_seconds.title: Window Seconds
window_seconds.description: the length of the window, in seconds

retry_after_seconds.title: Retry After Seconds
retry_after_seconds.description: the most you need to wait, in seconds. The API's own limit also sends it as the `Retry-After` header; the edge's per-address limit sends it only here

lookups_used.title: Lookups Used
lookups_used.description: requests counted in the current window

RateLimited.title: RateLimited
RateLimited.description: HTTP 429: over a per-caller limit. Returned only while a limit is in force; wait `retry_after_seconds`.

party_record_id.title: Party Record Id
party_record_id.description: identifies this record in the registration data. Not a person ID: one person usually has several records

key_name.title: Key Name
key_name.description: the part of the name the record is filed under, usually the surname

names_before_key_name.title: Names Before Key Name
names_before_key_name.description: the rest of the name, usually given names

ipi_name_number.title: Ipi Name Number
ipi_name_number.description: the IPI name number, or null when the record has none

persistent_id.title: Persistent Id
persistent_id.description: the person ID this record belongs to, or null. It can differ from the candidate's `persistent_id` when this lookup groups a record that the stored person does not hold

prerelease.title: Prerelease
prerelease.description: true: the ID may stop resolving, or later point at a different person, without notice, so do not store it. False: a released ID. Null when there is no ID

Record.title: Record
Record.description: One registration record: a name as it was registered, with its IPI name number if it has one.

code.title: Code
code.description: `single-token`: the name is one word, which is not searched. `no-match`: nothing matched closely enough. `publishers-only`: every match is registered only as a publisher or administrator, not as a writer

nearest.title: Nearest
nearest.description: up to five registered names closest to the one asked for, as spelling suggestions; often empty

set_aside_roles.title: Set Aside Roles
set_aside_roles.description: for `publishers-only`, the roles of the records set aside: `publisher`, `administrator`, or both

Rejection.title: Rejection
Rejection.description: Why a lookup stopped without candidates. It comes with HTTP 200: it is an answer, not an error.

refs.title: Refs
refs.description: the candidates the two records are in, by `ref`

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: `review_band`: the model was unsure, scoring at least `provenance.review_threshold` but below `query.threshold`. `middle_name_conflict`: the records give different middle names, and are never joined on the model alone. `generation_suffix_conflict`: the names carry different generations (JR and SR, II and III), and are never joined on the model alone. `korean_same_name_by_sound`: one Korean name written in different romanisations, held apart rather than joined on how it sounds. `blocked_would_join_conflicting_records`: joining would put two conflicting records into one person through a third, so it was held back whatever the probability

probability.title: Probability
probability.description: the model's calibrated probability that the two records are one person, from 0 to 1

shared.title: Shared
shared.description: what the two records have in common, under `co_writers`, `publishers` and `administrators`, each `{"count": n, "rarest": [names]}`. `rarest` lists the least common shared names, which say the most; names shared by a very large number of writers are left out. A key may be absent

ReviewItem.title: ReviewItem
ReviewItem.description: A pair of records that was NOT joined. Nothing here is part of any candidate: show it apart from `candidates`.

name.title: Name
name.description: the name it is registered under

ipi_name_number.title: Ipi Name Number
ipi_name_number.description: its IPI name number, if it has one

persistent_id.title: Persistent Id
persistent_id.description: the person ID holding this record, if any

tier.title: Tier
tier.description: `same_name`: the name matches as a lookup's would, beyond the records the lookup compared. `half_name`: only the given name or the surname matches, as with a stage name; offered only for a title few works share

titles.title: Titles
titles.description: its works with this exact title, as registered; at most three

SongBeyond.title: SongBeyond
SongBeyond.description: A writer the song reached that the name did not. Shown beside the answer, never joined to anyone in it.

match.title: Match
match.description: `exact`: a work has this title. `partial`: no exact title, but the song's words appear whole and in order in one (`hurt` in `HURT SO GOOD`), which is weaker evidence. `none`: no one in this answer has a work by that title. `too_short`: the song has no letters or digits to match on

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: refs of the candidates holding a match, in the order of `candidates`

records.title: Records
records.description: the matching records, with their titles

beyond.title: Beyond
beyond.description: writers with a work by this exact title whom the name did not find; empty when `beyond_status` is not `ok`

beyond_status.title: Beyond Status
beyond_status.description: null when this search did not run. `ok`: it ran. `none`: no work has this exact title. `common`: too many works share the title to point at anyone. `unavailable`: not offered here yet

SongMatch.title: SongMatch
SongMatch.description:
Which of this answer's people wrote a work with the song's title. `candidates` and `records` only point at
people already in the answer and never change who is grouped with whom. `beyond`, when present, lists writers
the song reached that the name did not, kept apart from the answer.

titles.title: Titles
titles.description: its matching work titles, as registered; at most three

SongRecord.title: SongRecord
SongRecord.description: A record in this answer with a work by the song's title.

version.title: Version
version.description: the release, as in the site's small print. Two deploys of one release can carry different models, which is what `model_md5` is for

mlc_snapshot.title: Mlc Snapshot
mlc_snapshot.description: the date of the registration-data release this answer read, YYYY-MM-DD. Null when that load is undated: never a guess

review_threshold.title: Review Threshold
review_threshold.description: the lowest probability at which an unjoined pair is listed in `review`

max_candidates.title: Max Candidates
max_candidates.description: the most records one lookup groups

VersionResponse.title: VersionResponse
VersionResponse.description: What is serving: the release, the model and the settings every lookup uses.

total.title: Total
total.description: all the person's works: distinct works across member records, a work under two of them counted once

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: the position of the first work on this page

next_offset.title: Next Offset
next_offset.description: pass as `works_offset` for the next page; null on the last page

ordered_by.title: Ordered By
ordered_by.description: `recordings` when these works are ordered by how many recordings each has, `coded` when that count is not available and the page falls back to works with an ISWC first

WorksPage.title: WorksPage
WorksPage.description: One page of the person's works: most-recorded first when recording counts are available (see `ordered_by`).

ipi_name_number.title: Ipi Name Number
ipi_name_number.description: the number, as 11 digits with its leading zeros. For an `invalid` entry, the text as sent, cut to 32 characters

status.title: Status
status.description: `person`: one person holds this number. `several`: more than one person holds it, and none is chosen. `none`: no person here holds it; it may belong to a publisher, or its records have not been grouped. `invalid`: not an IPI name number (up to 11 digits; spaces and dashes are ignored)

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: the person's ID, `SLP-XXXX-XXXX-C`; null unless `status` is `person`

name.title: Name
name.description: the name to show for the person; null unless `status` is `person`

names.title: Names
names.description: every distinct name the person's records are registered under, `name` first. Compare a spelling you hold against it: a spelling not in this list is not one this person is registered under. Empty unless `status` is `person`

works.title: Works
works.description: distinct works across the person's records; null unless `status` is `person`

main_ipi_name_number.title: Main Ipi Name Number
main_ipi_name_number.description: the person's main number: the one on the record their ID was created around. It can differ from `ipi_name_number`: the number sent may be a secondary one

works_on_main_ipi.title: Works On Main Ipi
works_on_main_ipi.description: distinct works on the records carrying `main_ipi_name_number`

works_elsewhere.title: Works Elsewhere
works_elsewhere.description: `works` minus `works_on_main_ipi`: works registered only under another spelling of the name or another IPI name number. Null when `works_on_main_ipi` is

persons.title: Persons
persons.description: how many persons hold this number: 1 for `person`, 2 or more for `several`, 0 otherwise

person_url.title: Person Url
person_url.description: the page to open, relative to this site: the person's page, or for `several` the page listing everyone who holds the number

WriterAnswer.title: WriterAnswer
WriterAnswer.description: One IPI name number from the list, and the person who holds it.

writers.title: Writers
writers.description: one entry per distinct number, in the order first sent

rate_limit.description: your remaining allowance; null when no per-caller limit is in force

WritersResponse.title: WritersResponse
WritersResponse.description:
The writers behind a list of IPI name numbers, in the order sent, and how each one's works divide between
their main number and the rest.

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.description: distinct entries checked, invalid ones included

several.title: Several
several.description: numbers held by more than one person

invalid.title: Invalid
invalid.description: entries that are not IPI name numbers

persons.title: Persons
persons.description: distinct persons found. Two numbers of one writer count once

with_works_elsewhere.title: With Works Elsewhere
with_works_elsewhere.description: of `persons`, how many have `works_elsewhere` above zero: writers with works registered under another spelling or number

WritersSummary.title: WritersSummary
WritersSummary.description: Totals over the list. Each number is counted once, however many times it was sent.

tags.name: Lookup
tags.description: Find the people who write under a name.

tags.name: Persons
tags.description: Read stored persons, by person ID or by IPI name number.

tags.name: Service
tags.description: What is serving, and whether it is up.
